patient.name: Gerald Whitmore
patient.chief_complaint: Progressive numbness and weakness in feet and hands over 18 months, worse in the morning
patient.hpi: Gerald Whitmore is a 58-year-old accountant with a 16-year history of type 2 diabetes presenting with 18 months of progressive bilateral foot and hand numbness and weakness. He initially noticed burning discomfort in both feet that has evolved into dense numbness. He also notes increasing difficulty with fine motor tasks in both hands, particularly loosening jar lids, and has noted significant weakness when ascending stairs and rising from low chairs. He reports that the symptoms are distinctly worse in the morning with some looseness and improvement through the day — a pattern he has noted consistently. His diabetes was described as 'under good control' by his primary care physician with an HbA1c of 7.1% at his last check 6 months ago, and there has been no change in his diabetes medications. He does not take metformin (intolerant — GI side effects) and is on glipizide alone. B12 is therefore not a metformin-related concern. He denies alcohol use. He is on atorvastatin and has read online that statins can cause nerve problems, which he raises. Neurological examination reveals notable proximal weakness that he says has never been part of his prior neuropathy discussions. He is frustrated that two previous evaluations attributed symptoms to diabetic neuropathy without addressing the proximal weakness.
pmh: Prior lumbar disc herniation L4-L5 (conservatively managed, resolved)
patient.review_of_systems: Positive: bilateral hand/foot numbness and weakness, proximal leg weakness, morning stiffness of hands (30 minutes), difficulty with stairs. Negative: falls, bowel/bladder dysfunction, rash, fever, dry eyes, dry mouth, facial weakness, dysphagia.

medications.drug: Glipizide 10 mg twice daily (diabetes — metformin intolerant)

family_history: Father: type 2 diabetes. Mother: hypothyroidism. No family history of neuropathy.

social_history.note: Accountant at CPA firm. Married, 2 children. Non-smoker. Rare alcohol (2 glasses wine per week). No illicit drugs. No toxic occupational exposures.

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented x4. Normal cognition.
neurological_exam.motor: Proximal: hip flexors 4/5 bilaterally, hip abductors 4-/5 bilaterally. Knee extensors 4+/5 bilaterally. Shoulder abductors 4+/5 bilaterally. Distal: dorsiflexion 4/5 bilaterally, intrinsic hand muscles 4/5 bilaterally. Grip 4/5 bilaterally.
neurological_exam.sensory: Reduced light touch and pinprick in stocking distribution to mid-shin bilaterally. Vibration markedly reduced at great toes (3 seconds), reduced at ankles (7 seconds). Proprioception mildly reduced bilateral great toes. Bilateral hand fingertip numbness with mild reduction in vibration.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Biceps 2+ bilaterally, triceps 1+ bilaterally. Patellar 1+ bilaterally. Achilles absent bilaterally.
neurological_exam.coordination: Dysmetria on finger-nose test bilaterally, mild. Heel-shin intact. Romberg positive.
neurological_exam.gait: Mildly wide-based with slight steppage. Tandem impaired. Trendelenburg sign bilateral on single-leg stance — proximal hip weakness.
neurological_exam.special_tests: No Babinski. No clonus. Morning hand stiffness noted by patient. No synovial thickening on hand exam.

Neuropathy Workup.value: No M-spike; polyclonal IgG elevation 1,580 mg/dL

labs.interpretation: Abnormal values: Glucose 138 mg/dL (H), CK (creatine kinase) 148 U/L (H), HbA1c 7.1 % (H), Fasting glucose (AM) 138 mg/dL (H), ESR 24 mm/hr (H), SPEP No M-spike; polyclonal IgG elevation 1,580 mg/dL  (H), Rheumatoid Factor 128 IU/mL (H), Anti-CCP antibody 186 U/mL (H), CK (repeat) 152 U/L (H).

report.summary: ABNORMAL NCS/EMG. Primarily axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy. Proximal EMG involvement present. Pattern is consistent with mixed diabetic axonal neuropathy and RA-associated axonal polyneuropathy. No typical CIDP demyelinating pattern. No focal entrapment neuropathy at wrist (carpal tunnel) or elbow (cubital tunnel).

motor.flag: mildly prolonged DML, reduced amplitude, mildly slow velocity — axonal pattern

motor.nerve: Right Ulnar Motor (wrist, below elbow, above elbow)

sensory.flag: reduced amplitude and velocity — axonal pattern
mildly reduced amplitude — no carpal tunnel pattern

emg.summary: Axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy with proximal muscle involvement (vastus lateralis, deltoid). Proximal EMG changes are not typical for purely diabetic axonal neuropathy. Velocities not severely slowed (>75% LLN) — not classical CIDP. Pattern: axonal polyneuropathy with proximal involvement, raising RA-associated neuropathy, or mixed diabetic + RA.

report.overall_impression: AXONAL SENSORIMOTOR POLYNEUROPATHY with proximal involvement. The proximal EMG findings and clinical morning stiffness warrant autoimmune workup beyond standard diabetic neuropathy evaluation. Anti-CCP/RF results (from labs) confirm RA diagnosis, which is likely the dominant neuropathy etiology.

report.summary: Sural nerve biopsy: axonal degeneration, mildly reduced myelinated fiber density. No vasculitis. No significant inflammatory infiltrate. Findings: axonal neuropathy without vasculitis — consistent with RA-associated non-vasculitic axonal polyneuropathy superimposed on diabetic background. Disease-modifying therapy for RA is indicated.
report.histology: Myelinated fiber density moderately reduced. Axonal degeneration, Wallerian degeneration pattern. No epineurial vasculitis (no transmural inflammation, no fibrinoid necrosis). No perivascular lymphocytic aggregates. No amyloid (Congo red negative). No granulomas.
report.interpretation: Non-vasculitic RA neuropathy — axonal polyneuropathy in context of established RA (confirmed by labs). Prognosis: good response expected with RA disease-modifying therapy (methotrexate + biologic if needed). No vasculitic neuropathy requiring high-dose steroids/cyclophosphamide.

report.summary: X-ray bilateral hands and wrists: periarticular osteopenia at MCP joints bilaterally. Subtle joint space narrowing at bilateral 2nd-3rd MCP joints. No frank erosions on plain film. Findings early-moderate RA pattern. MRI hands recommended for erosion detection if clinical management requires.
report.interpretation: Periarticular osteopenia and subtle narrowing consistent with early-moderate seropositive RA. Anti-CCP 186 U/mL + RF 128 IU/mL + periarticular osteopenia = seropositive erosive RA. DMARD initiation indicated — typically methotrexate 15-20 mg weekly + folic acid.

output.procedure: Lumbar puncture — performed to exclude CIDP given proximal EMG involvement

output.test_type: Upper Extremity Focused NCS — Entrapment Neuropathy Screen

report.summary: Targeted upper extremity NCS to evaluate carpal tunnel syndrome and cubital tunnel syndrome given hand symptoms. Results: No carpal tunnel syndrome (median palmar latency normal, no median-ulnar palmar latency difference). No cubital tunnel syndrome (ulnar motor across elbow velocity 52.8 m/s, normal). Findings consistent with diffuse polyneuropathy affecting hand intrinsics rather than focal entrapment.

median_ulnar_comparison.flag: normal (<0.4 ms threshold for carpal tunnel)

report.interpretation: No evidence of carpal tunnel syndrome or cubital tunnel syndrome. Hand numbness and intrinsic weakness are from diffuse polyneuropathy, not focal entrapment.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Rheumatoid arthritis-associated peripheral neuropathy (axonal polyneuropathy) in a patient with type 2 diabetes
critical_actions: Order anti-CCP antibody — morning stiffness and proximal weakness should trigger RA workup in neuropathy evaluation
Nerve biopsy to differentiate vasculitic from non-vasculitic RA neuropathy (determines treatment intensity)
Address patient concern about statins with CK + anti-HMGCR testing — do NOT simply discontinue statin without evidence
Initiate DMARD therapy through rheumatology — RA-associated neuropathy responds to RA disease control
Do not over-attribute all findings to diabetes — anti-CCP 186 is specific for RA and demands diagnosis
contraindicated_actions: Do not discontinue atorvastatin without evidence of statin neuropathy — CK and anti-HMGCR are normal
Do not diagnose as pure diabetic neuropathy and miss treatable RA
Do not start cyclophosphamide/high-dose steroids for vasculitic neuropathy — nerve biopsy shows no vasculitis
Do not give symptomatic treatment only without DMARD initiation for active RA with erosive disease

differential.key_distinguishing: HbA1c 7.1% explains mild length-dependent axonal component; does NOT explain proximal weakness, morning stiffness, highly positive anti-CCP/RF, or MRI synovitis
CK normal, anti-HMGCR negative; statin neuropathy is rare and primarily myopathic; discontinuing statin would miss the real RA diagnosis
NCS shows axonal predominance not demyelinating velocities; CSF protein only mildly elevated (52 mg/dL); CIDP does not cause morning stiffness or joint symptoms
Nerve biopsy shows no vasculitis — non-vasculitic RA neuropathy; would not require cyclophosphamide; methotrexate DMARD therapy appropriate

key_reasoning_points: MODERATE DIFFICULTY: Anchoring bias on 16-year diabetes history — easy to attribute everything to diabetic neuropathy
KEY CLUE 1: Morning stiffness >30 minutes in someone presenting as 'neuropathy' should trigger anti-CCP/RF testing
KEY CLUE 2: Proximal weakness (vastus lateralis on EMG) is NOT a feature of typical diabetic length-dependent axonal neuropathy
KEY CLUE 3: Patient raised statin concern — must be taken seriously and formally evaluated (CK, anti-HMGCR) rather than dismissed
RA neuropathy is underrecognized — seropositive RA patients with inadequate disease control develop axonal polyneuropathy
Nerve biopsy differentiates vasculitic (requires cyclophosphamide) from non-vasculitic (methotrexate DMARD) RA neuropathy
Statin neuropathy trap: common patient belief, must be formally excluded to reassure and prevent unnecessary discontinuation of cardiovascular-protective medication
